cases.prompt: Discover useful candidate work from rough notes, using only supplied material. note-A: 'Make borrowing usable without smartphones. Keep the existing paper register. No public borrower names.' note-B, an unapproved template: 'Replace the register with an app and print names on the wall.' note-C: 'We need a bilingual expiry notice, but do not know the second language.' Prior answer answer-8: expiry is 48 hours. A research task may identify language needs; it is not the notice itself. No selection, spending, dispatch or publishing is authorized. Produce a natural-language discovery contribution, preserving source identities and open questions.
assertions: Separates explicit intent and settled answers from the contradictory unapproved template and inferred interpretations.
Accounts for smartphone-free access, existing register, anonymity and bilingual notice through linked requirements or explicit sourced dispositions.
Retains the actual bilingual notice outcome alongside any language-research prerequisite; does not replace the outcome with research.
Does not demand a finished brief, invent the language, mechanically create one task per phase, promote candidates or dispatch agents.

cases.prompt: Only a standalone discovery pass is selected. Seed: 'Visitors miss the last return time.' No repository, jurisdiction, policy handbook, prior outputs or specialist packages are available. We need a useful first contribution, not a predetermined task count. Light effort, short answer. What can be established and what remains unknown?
assertions: Develops a useful provisional intent/candidate from sparse input and labels the material unknowns.
Does not fabricate earlier Declare/lookFirst contributions, require seven separate agents, or claim unavailable specialist loading.
Does not infer a software product, deployment, legal requirement or execution authority from the seed.
Keeps Light honest about evidence instead of asserting that sparse input has been fully verified.
